messages.subject: Re: Multilevel sem with variables only on level-1
parts:
Try this advice from the linked page (the second part, but also read the first):

  • you must specify a model for each level; the following syntax is not allowed and will produce an error:

•   model <- '
      level: 1
          fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3
      level: 2
  '

• if you do not have a model in mind for level 2, you can specify a saturated level by adding all variances and covariances of the endogenous variables (here: y1, y2 and y3):

      model <- '
      level: 1
          fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3
      level: 2
          y1 ~~ y1 + y2 + y3
          y2 ~~ y2 + y3
          y3 ~~ y3
  '

Try this advice from the linked page (the second part, but also read the first):

  • you must specify a model for each level; the following syntax is not allowed and will produce an error:

  •   model <- '
      level: 1
          fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3
      level: 2
  '

  • if you do not have a model in mind for level 2, you can specify a saturated level by adding all variances and covariances of the endogenous variables (here: y1, y2 and y3):

      model <- '
      level: 1
          fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3
          fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3
      level: 2
          y1 ~~ y1 + y2 + y3
          y2 ~~ y2 + y3
          y3 ~~ y3
  '
